hsp_text: Failure/recovery acceptance covers concurrent same-content captures, crash after fetch/before commit, 429s, timeouts, truncated bytes, transcript failures, outage abstention, cursor replay, ACL non-leakage, backup restore, exact-hash approval binding, 0/1/16 MiB source limits, base64 wire overhead, digest mismatch, held-FD nofollow regular-file TOCTOU checks, the Slice 3C1 local clear-manifest PHI gate and pre-acceptance refusal, unsupported-media/encoding invalidation before scanner evaluation, future-slice bounded non-PHI quarantine, and ambiguous record/event/lineage recovery.
hsp_assert_text: Fixture: the complete fault matrix and portable backup. Test/command: `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 uv run pytest -p no:cacheprovider` plus recovery/fault integration suite. Assert: no loss, no unauthorized disclosure, no `SOURCE` path/base64/kind persistence, no downstream duplicate effect, preserved IDs/lineage after restore, supported-but-unattested source is `400`/`source_refused`, scanner/manifest error is `503`, no raw bytes on 3C1 refusal, and approval rejection on any hash drift. Retain: full pytest log, fault matrix, restored-store verification, and approval failure report.
notes: Every HSP-12 demand row below is proved by an existing test, a new test in tests/test_e5_fault_matrix.py, or both. One row (backup restore / crash recovery for the transcribe lane) surfaced a pre-existing production defect in houndd/projection.py that this file does not own and does not fix; it is pinned as a strict xfail (test_e5_backup_restore_drill_including_a_completed_transcription_KNOWN_DEFECT) so the suite stays green while the gap stays impossible to silently regress-hide. See known_defects below.

demands.why_new: Prior 429 coverage is either a bare AdapterFailed injection via a fake host, or hound_web_adapters.whisper.transcribe() called standalone; nothing drove a real 429 through AdapterHost.from_env + CommitRuntime.execute_adapter end to end.

Genuinely missing case: a real Whisper 429 flowing through the full commit path (capture binding, real AdapterHost.from_env wiring, durable failed record, journal, verify_store), not a fake-host exception injection.

Consolidates outage abstention across every adapter operation (search/url/transcribe) in one pass using the real credential-derived AdapterHost.from_env({}) houndd binds at startup, and asserts no credential material leaks into durable state -- prior coverage was per-operation and scattered.

No prior test built a live-shaped store with the commit runtime, copied it, destroyed the original outright, and proved verify_store green plus journal.query serving identical results from the copy alone. The drill covers ingest.file, import.record, ingest.media, and ingest.search cleanly. Extending it to a completed transcription surfaced known_defects[0] below; that lane is pinned as a strict xfail rather than silently dropped from the matrix.

Prior coverage of collision-on-changed-request only existed for ingest.file and ingest.media. The three adapter operations -- ingest.search, ingest.url, transcribe -- had zero collision-on-drift coverage anywhere in the suite. This test consolidates hash-drift rejection across all six commit operations in one place.

known_defects.title: Projection rebuild (and therefore houndd startup recovery) crashes after any completed transcription
known_defects.pinned_as: strict xfail (test fails loudly -- XPASS -- the moment the bug is fixed, forcing removal of the marker)
known_defects.description: _derive_rows() treats every completed outcome whose object_key does not start with 'legacy:' as blob-backed, and unconditionally calls records.blobs.get(content_sha256). A completed transcription's object_key is 'transcript:<hash>'; by VISION design (B5), transcript bytes are never staged as a blob. The lookup raises houndd.store.UnsafeStoreError. Because HounddService.__init__ calls store.recover() -> Projection.rebuild() at startup (HSP-20's mandatory startup recovery), houndd fails to boot against its own state root after the first completed transcription anywhere in its journal -- not merely a rebuild-index maintenance-route edge case, a daemon boot crash. The live incrementally-maintained projection is also affected: verify_store(state) (projection=True, default) reports 'projection drift' as invalid for the same reason, without crashing, immediately after a completed transcribe commit under normal operation.
known_defects.impact: Blocks the HSP-12 backup-restore claim and the HSP-20 crash-recovery claim for the transcribe lane specifically. Any live deployment that completes even one transcription and then restarts houndd will not come back up.
known_defects.fix: Add a third branch in _derive_rows alongside the existing 'legacy:' branch: skip the blob lookup for object_key.startswith('transcript:') (or generalize to any adapter operation outside ADAPTER_MEDIA_TYPES that stages no content), matching commit_runtime.py's own '_plan_requires_content' logic used to decide whether to stage a blob in the first place.
known_defects.owner: unassigned -- out of tests/test_e5_fault_matrix.py's file ownership; needs routing to whoever owns src/houndd/projection.py or the B5/transcribe lane
known_defects.status: FIXED 2026-08-04: projection._derive_rows and _DERIVED_BLOB_KEYS gained the transcript: branch; tripwire test flipped to a live green assertion in the same commit.
